scope:
Count pinned original NetLog sends without exporting URLs or credentials.

Counts are observed outgoing transaction-header emissions, not policy, cache hits,
successful responses or unique logical requests. Diagnostic --disable-quic runs
are separated from captures without that flag.
captureProvenance: Five existing pinned original Spotify NetLogs. The upload-http2 capture is independently documented as a deliberate --disable-quic run; raw command-line flags are reduced to booleans here.

altSvcChronology.binding: ALT_SVC_FOUND events are attributed through URL request source -> HTTP_STREAM_JOB_CONTROLLER_BOUND source_dependency. No arbitrary graph or hostname coalescing inference.
altSvcChronology.limits: First observed advertisement is a final logged response, not proof of first learning. Cached/persisted alternatives may predate capture. DNS_ALPN absence is log coverage, not proof that DNS never influences protocol selection.

limits: No raw URL, query, credential, identity, header value, body, private command line/profile path or credential hash is exported.
Counts are actual HTTP_TRANSACTION_*_SEND_REQUEST_HEADERS emissions. Retries/redirects can yield multiple sends; cache hits and requests with no outgoing header event are excluded.
H2/H3 event names establish observed HTTP protocol; H1 rows come from HTTP_TRANSACTION_SEND_REQUEST_HEADERS. Counts are not a unique-request or success census.
No Login5/client-token/image-map send in these retained runs means missing coverage, not unsupported HTTP or a selection policy. Account OAuth token refresh does not prove fresh sign-in flow.

No explicit QUIC force/disable flag is a limited launch fact, not proof of factory-default state: persisted Alt-Svc/server properties, DNS, network reachability and Chromium experiments are not reconstructed.
Forced-H2 diagnostic counts must not be merged into claims about default protocol selection.
A shared QUIC session is proved only by matching original source_dependency session IDs at the send. It does not prove requests share a body, track, consumer or admission purpose.
Route families intentionally remove identities and queries. Their counts do not verify exact methods/headers/body/query bytes, connection selection policy or transport fingerprint equivalence.
Unclassified spclient routes remain explicit counts and are not assigned a guessed family.
No network, original app/profile/process, live Flutter action, transport/runtime edit, general test or formatter action.
